He that rejoyces not at your return  In safety, is mine enemy for ever.

arxiv-2108-10653.title: Aspects of Coulomb gases
arxiv-2108-10653.creator: Djalil Chafaï
arxiv-2108-10653.description: Abstract . Coulomb gases are special probability distributions, related to potential theory, that appear at many places in pure and applied mathematics and physics. In these short expository notes, we focus on some models, ideas, and structures. We present briefly selected mathematical aspects, mostly related to exact solvability and first and second order global asymptotics.

arxiv-2109-02596.title: scikit-dimension: a Python package for intrinsic dimension estimation
arxiv-2109-02596.creator: Jonathan Bac *, Evgeny M. Mirkes, Alexander N. Gorban \orcidG, Ivan Tyukin, Andrei Zinovyev*
arxiv-2109-02596.description: Abstract Dealing with uncertainty in applications of machine learning to real-life data critically depends on the knowledge of intrinsic dimensionality (ID). A number of methods have been suggested for the purpose of estimating ID, but no standard package to easily apply them one by one or all at once has been implemented in Python.

arxiv-2203-13775.title: Interlopers speak out: studying the dark universe using small-scale lensing anisotropies 2022 Interlopers speak out: studying the dark universe using small-scale lensing anisotropies – D
arxiv-2203-13775.creator: Birendra Dhanasingham, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Benson, and Daniel Gilman
arxiv-2203-13775.description: Abstract Strongly lensed systems are powerful probes of the distribution of dark matter on small scales. In this paper, we show that line-of-sight haloes between the source and the observers give rise to a distinct anisotropic signature in the two-point function of the effective lensing deflection field.

arxiv-2304-10655.title: The Dataset Multiplicity Problem: How Unreliable Data Impacts Predictions
arxiv-2304-10655.creator: Anna P. Meyer, Aws Albarghouthi, Loris D’Antoni
arxiv-2304-10655.description: Abstract We introduce dataset multiplicity, a way to study how inaccuracies, uncertainty, and social bias in training datasets impact test-time predictions. The dataset multiplicity framework asks a counterfactual question of what the set of resultant models (and associated test-time predictions) would be if we could somehow access all hypothetical, unbiased versions of the dataset.

arxiv-2412-08623.title: A 1% accurate method to include baryonic effects in galaxy-galaxy lensing models
arxiv-2412-08623.creator: M. Zennaro, G. Aricò, C. García-García, R. E. Angulo, L. Ondaro-Mallea, S. Contreras, A. Nicola, M. Schaller, J. Schaye
arxiv-2412-08623.description: Abstract Context. The clustering of galaxies and galaxy-galaxy lensing are two of the main observational probes in Stage-IV large-scale structure surveys, such as Euclid and LSST. Unfortunately, the complicated relationship between galaxies and matter greatly limits the exploitation of this data.

arxiv-2503-21834.title: A Multi-Modal Knowledge-Enhanced Framework for Vessel Trajectory Prediction
arxiv-2503-21834.creator: Haomin Yu, Tianyi Li ∗ , Kristian Torp, Christian S. Jensen
arxiv-2503-21834.description: Abstract . Accurate vessel trajectory prediction facilitates improved navigational safety, routing, and environmental protection. However, existing prediction methods are challenged by the irregular sampling time intervals of the vessel tracking data from the global AIS system and the complexity of vessel movement. These aspects render model learning and generalization difficult.

arxiv-2508-18392.title: Dynamic System Optimum: A Projection-based Framework for Macroscopic Traffic Models
arxiv-2508-18392.creator: Mostafa Ameli, Sérgio F. A. Batista, Jean-Patrick Lebacque, Mónica Menéndez
arxiv-2508-18392.description: Abstract This paper proposes the theoretical grounds for emulating the Dynamic System Optimum with desired arrival times on regional networks, using aggregated traffic dynamics based on the Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram. We used a projection gradient-based solution method that avoids the need to compute approximations of marginal travel times.

arxiv-2602-21308.title: Automatic Identification of Compounds in Molecular Mixtures from Liquid-Phase Infrared Spectra
arxiv-2602-21308.creator: Yannah J.U. Melle, 1,2 Thanh Nguyen, 3 Jeffrey Lopez, 3,∗ Daniel Schwalbe-Koda 1,∗ 1 Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of California, Los Angeles, CA, USA 2 Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of California, Los Angeles, CA, USA 3 Department of Chemical and
arxiv-2602-21308.description: Abstract Interpreting spectroscopy data is a critical bottleneck in automating chemical research and industrial characterization. Particularly within infrared (IR) spectroscopy, identifying compounds in complex, liquid-phase chemical mixtures largely relies on expert knowledge, as variable peak assignment, broadening, and shifts hinder data-driven methods.

arxiv-2603-06764.title: Efficient Classical Simulation of Low-Rank-Width Quantum Circuits Using ZX-Calculus
arxiv-2603-06764.creator: Fedor Kuyanov and Aleks Kissinger

plos-pone-0003986.title: CD8+ T-Cell Interleukin-7 Receptor Alpha Expression as a Potential Indicator of Disease Status in HIV-Infected Children
plos-pone-0003986.creator: Tanvi S. Sharma, Jane Hughes, Amarylis Murillo et al.
plos-pone-0003986.description: PLOS ONE research article. Initiation and modification of antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected children depend on viral load and CD4+ T-cell count. However, these surrogates have limitations, and complementary immunological markers to assess therapeutic response are needed. Our aim was to evaluate CD8+ T

pmc-10580135.title: Individualized Virtual Reality for Increasing Self-Compassion: Evaluation Study
pmc-10580135.creator: Ilona Halim, Lehan Stemmet, Sylvia Hach, Richard Porter, Hai-Ning Liang, Atiyeh Vaezipour, Julie D Henry, Nilufar Baghaei, John Torous, Neelesh Mungoli, Elena Korshakova
pmc-10580135.description: BackgroundDepression and anxiety are common and debilitating mental disorders with severe negative repercussions at both individual and societal levels. Although virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a safe and effective tool for the treatment of anxiety disorders, studies of the therapeutic application of VR to treat depression are more limited.

pmc-10758648.title: Dual primary gastric and colorectal cancer: A complex challenge in surgical oncology
pmc-10758648.creator: Luigi Marano
pmc-10758648.description: The intricate interplay of colorectal cancer (CRC) and gastric cancer (GC) as dual primary malignancies presents a significant challenge in surgical oncology. CRC is the most common secondary malignancy in GC patients, and vice versa, evidence highlighted by advances in diagnostic procedures and therapy modalities that impact patient survival.

pmc-11402492.title: Development of Subcutaneous Panniculitis-Like T-cell Lymphoma After Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Treatment
pmc-11402492.creator: Tommy Y Yu, Zartash Gul, Alicia M Hunt, Michael J Williams, Alexander M Maley
pmc-11402492.description: Program death 1 (PD-1) inhibitors such as nivolumab are immune checkpoint inhibitors that have revolutionized the treatment of metastatic melanoma. Despite its success in treating melanoma, immune activation can lead to immune-related adverse effects, which are experienced by half of melanoma patients treated with PD-1 inhibitors.

pmc-11505151.title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Characterization of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. Isolates from Pigs at Slaughterhouse and from Commercial Pork Meat in Portugal
pmc-11505151.creator: Carlota Gonçalves, Leonor Silveira, João Rodrigues, Rosália Furtado, Sónia Ramos, Alexandra Nunes, Ângela Pista, David Rodríguez-Lázaro
pmc-11505151.description: Background: Foodborne diseases are a serious public health concern, and food-producing animals are a major source of contamination. Methods: The present study analysed Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. isolated from faecal samples of 100 fattening pigs and from 52 samples of pork meat.

pmc-11567111.title: Sustainability and nutritional composition of food offer and choices in three hospital canteens in Italy
pmc-11567111.creator: Diana Menis, Federica Fiori, Peter Cautero, Daniela Zago, Yvonne Beorchia, Lorenzo Dallan, Pietro Vettorazzo, Lucia Lesa, Alessandro Conte, Enrico Scarpis, Laura Brunelli, Maria Parpinel
pmc-11567111.description: Diet is considered one of the most important determinants of health and at the same time a cause of climate change. We conducted a cross-sectional study in three Italian hospital canteens on five consecutive working days to investigate food offer availability and user choices in terms of nutritional intake and environmental impact.

pmc-11629541.title: Molecular targets and mechanisms of Sijunzi decoction in the treatment of Parkinson’s disease: evidence from network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation
pmc-11629541.creator: Yang Jiang, Wanfeng Wu, Le Xie, Yue Zhou, Kailin Yang, Dahua Wu, Wenfeng Xu, Rui Fang, Jinwen Ge
pmc-11629541.description: AimTo explore the molecular mechanism of Sijunzi Decoction (SJZD) in the treatment of Parkinson’s disease (PD) through the application of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, complemented by experimental verification.MethodsThe BATMAN-TCM, GeneCards, and DisGeNet databases were searched to screen the active components and therapeutic targets of SJZD. pmc-12429980.title: Inner Dialogues and Nutritional Anxiety in Sports Tourism: Understanding Runners’ Habits in Pre-Race Food-Related Stress Abroad
pmc-12429980.creator: Mateusz Rozmiarek, Daniel Graham
pmc-12429980.description: Background/Objectives: For runners competing abroad in sports events, the hours before a race are marked by heightened psychological tension, where even food choices can feel crucial to success. While pre-race nutrition is often addressed in terms of physiological needs, little is known about the inner psychological processes that accompany food decisions in unfamiliar cultural and environmental contexts.

pmc-12852810.title: Early prediction of alopecia areata using machine learning modeling of neuro stress immune signatures from multi datasets
pmc-12852810.creator: Anxin Chen, Lin Shang, Yingjiao Ju, Fenglin Zhuo
pmc-12852810.description: Alopecia areata (AA) is an easy-recurring disease that presents huge challenges globally. An efficient clinical tool to predict AA onset would be valuable for timely intervention. We extracted six AA-related datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). GO, KEGG, GSEA, GSVA and CIBERSORT algorithm were performed to elucidate the characteristics of AA.

pmc-13574276.title: Prioritising modifiable risk factors for self-management of urinary incontinence in older men: integrating expert consensus with patient readiness
pmc-13574276.creator: Olawunmi Olagundoye, Thomas F Monaghan, William Gibson, Adrian Wagg
pmc-13574276.description: BackgroundUrinary incontinence (UI) affects up to one-third of men aged ≥65 years, yet evidence to guide the selection of targets for self-management interventions remains limited. Although many contributing risk factors are potentially modifiable, little is known about which are considered clinically important by experts and are also viewed by older men as feasible and worthwhile to address.

pmc-13625675.title: Political cost, value balance, and the optimization of university public health emergency governance: an evolutionary game and small signal analysis
pmc-13625675.creator: Rui Wang, Haonan Wu, Yingyan Liu, Jianlin Li, Xin Li, Ruihao Li
pmc-13625675.description: In major public-health emergencies, universities constitute core nodes within a multi-actor intersecting governance network composed of governments, universities, students, media and social-sector organizations. While uniform closed-campus management can maximize the protection of students' physical health, it frequently overlooks students' mental-health needs and value-recognition concerns, which may exacerbate tensions between universities and students.

pmc-13660812.title: Sub‐Nanometer Curvature Unlocks Quantum Orbital Flexoelectricity in Graphene
pmc-13660812.creator: Sathvik Ajay Iyengar, James G McHugh, Jonathan P Salvage, Robert Vajtai, Venkataramana Gadhamshetty, Alan B Dalton, Manoj Tripathi, Pulickel M Ajayan, Vincent Meunier
pmc-13660812.description: Flexoelectricity, defined as polarization induced by strain gradients, is especially pronounced in two‐dimensional (2D) materials due to their mechanical flexibility and sensitivity to deformation. In nanostructures with nanometer‐scale curvature, bending can perturb out‐of‐plane π orbitals and generate quantum‐mechanical polarization and electrostatic modulation beyond classical lattice distortion alone.
